summary.title: Toren
summary.pov: Third-person limited (centered on Toren). The narrative voice tracks Toren's internal calculations and sensory processing while maintaining an objective distance from Rook's interiority until the final scene where Toren observes him.
summary.synopsis: The group arrives at Hobb's Wall. They negotiate with weighmaster Nell Quill for shelter, work placements, and passage to Meridian. Toren attempts to trade his family Ember (a Voss artifact) as currency; Nell reveals it is worthless without a specific user history (
summary.openingState: dead thing off a boy who doesn't know it's dead). When the board cannot place everyone together or save Senna, Rook refuses to be sold by Toren. Toren counters with an offer: trade Rook's labor for one season in exchange for keeping the group united and saving their grandmother. Nell accepts this arrangement conditionally. The chapter ends with a non-combat training session where Rook teaches them situational awareness through forced fear responses.
turningPoints: Toren realizes his father's Ember is worthless as currency, only to be useful if held by the right person (Rook).
Nell Quill rejects Toren's offer of the stone but accepts Rook's labor in exchange for keeping the group together.
The shift from 'cargo' to a cohesive unit: The children refuse to stay without each other; Rook refuses to be priced.
summary.closingState: Toren is exhausted, emotionally raw (eyes streaming but voice steady), and carrying the weight of his father's sacrifice. He has successfully negotiated for their unity but feels he made a fool of himself with the stone. The group is now bound to Rook not by contract or payment, but by mutual survival necessity. They are moving north at dawn.

characters.name: Toren
characters.vocalBehavior: Steady, analytical, increasingly desperate then resolute. Starts with a voice holding 'nine days of held breath,' moves to a calculated offer, ends with raw emotion masked by physical stillness (streaming eyes but unshaking voice). Status: High stakes negotiation, shifting from naive trader to strategic leader.

characters.name: Rook
characters.vocalBehavior: Economical, low-status reserve masking high status. Uses short sentences and silence as weapons. When he speaks of being 'spent,' his voice drops to a quiet intensity that terrifies Toren more than shouting would. No anger in the tone, only absolute boundary-setting.

characters.name: Nell Quill
characters.vocalBehavior: Flat, rhythmic, transactional. Her voice is a ledger; she speaks in terms of 'yes/no' and arithmetic. When pity or respect surfaces ('That was well done'), it is brief and immediately suppressed back to the flat tone.

characters.name: Wyck
characters.vocalBehavior: Minimalist, physical presence over words. His silence in the negotiation carries more weight than his speech later (coloring when pushed). In training: functional, reactive.

characters.name: Senna
characters.vocalBehavior: Not present for dialogue; her absence is a character beat. Her condition drives the urgency of the negotiation (dying in a shed).

locations: Hobb's Wall (exterior): Described as a geography made of wrecks, forty feet high.
The Weigh-yard: Flat concrete apron with a beam scale and an awning. The site of the negotiation.
River Bend/Gravel Bar: Where Rook conducts training at dusk.
terms: Voss Ember (The Stone): A weapon/artifact that is worthless as currency unless held by a specific user; 'dead' in the wrong hands.
North Face: The dangerous construction side of the wall where people die.
Spring Convoy: Scheduled transport to Meridian, five months away.
Husks: Hostile entities encountered at the cut and during training.
summary.actionCadence: Slow/Heavy (Arrival) -> Tense/Staccato (Negotiation) -> Explosive/Crisis (The Ember reveal/Rook's refusal) -> Calm/Deliberate (Training). The pacing of Rook's training is methodical and repetitive, designed to induce a specific physiological state.
summary.emotionalRegister: Restraint. Characters suppress grief and fear in favor of survival logic. Toren feels 'colder' than grief; Rook displays 'pity' only briefly before returning to business.
narrationRisks: "It was much colder and much more useful than either." (Grief/Fear): Do not over-explain this emotion; let the narrator's voice remain flat while describing a complex internal state.

The Ember Reveal: The line "I'd be taking a dead thing off a boy who doesn't know it's dead" must land with absolute clarity. Rushing here loses the thematic weight of Toren's misunderstanding of his father's legacy.
"You don't get to spend me." (Rook): This is the emotional climax. It requires a pause before and after. Do not rush into Rook's anger; let the silence do the work.
The Training Instructions: The dialogue regarding 'shouting while frightened' must be delivered with clinical precision, not as an action movie instruction manual.
carryForward: Toren's realization that he misread his father and the Ember.
Rook's refusal to sign a contract but acceptance of the group.
The specific training technique (shouting while frightened) which will be tested immediately in Chapter 14.
